newsitem.title: USA: Exxon cites downstream, chemicals margins. [CORRECTED 15:52 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Exxon cites downstream, chemicals margins. [CORRECTED 15:52 GMT]

text.p: Exxon Corp said that improved margins in its refining and marketing division and its chemicals unit pushed it to the highest second quarter in its history and way ahead of the most optimistic analyst forecasts.

Overseas refining and marketing earnings rose to $382 million (corrects from $162 million) in the second quarter from $134.0 million (corrects from $98 million) a year ago, but the real surprise came in the U.S., where earnings rose to $162 million from $98.0 million.
Chemical earnings rose to $246 million in the U.S. from $166 million and to $147 million from $138 million overseas.
Over the half year, Exxon's U.S. refining and marketing earnings were $192 million from $82 million and $679 million from $324 million overseas.
"Downstream margins improved overall with U.S. and European industry refining margins recovering modestly from last year's depressed levels," the company said in a statement.
Second quarter chemical earnings rose to $246 million from $166 million in the U.S. and to $147 million from $138 million overseas.
In the six months there were $438 million, up from $319 million and $265 million from $272 million a year ago.

The company said that second quarter exploration and production earnings were hurt year on year by lower crude oil prices and domestic operations earnings fell to $335 million from $423 million, while overseas they were essentially flat at $620 million from $615 million.
Over the six month period, earnings were up in the U.S. at $889 million from $842 million and down overseas at $1.51 billion from $1.62 billion.
Exxon said that average crude prices were down $1.50 per barrel year on year and liquids production was 1.588 million barrels per day, down from 1.595 million.
While Canadian heavy oil and North Sea and Australian production were higher, maintenance, a revised production sharing agreement in Malaysia and field decline caused the drop in output.
Natural gas output was 5.64 billion cubic feet a day from 5.674 billion.
Petroleum product sales rose six percent to 5.348 million barrels per day and refinery throughput rose 121,000 barrels per day to 3.875 million bpd, due to lower maintenance.
Total net income was $1.965 billion in the second quarter, up from $1.57 billion and $4.14 billion for the first half, compared with $3.455 billion.
Revenues rose to $32.767 billion in the quarter from $32.311 billion and to $66.357 billion from $63.416 billion for the half.
